meta.title: Twenty years of Korean network history

events.title: 94% of households on broadband
events.note: The highest household broadband penetration in the OECD, four months before I was born.

events.title: WiBro launches in Seoul
events.note: Commercial mobile WiMAX, the first attempt at broadband away from the wall socket.

events.title: KCC votes to scrap WIPI
events.note: The domestic middleware mandate, in force since April 2005, had effectively barred foreign handsets from the market.

events.title: 45.6 million mobile subscribers
events.note: Over 93% of the population, in a country of 48.6 million.

events.title: WIPI mandate lifted
events.note: From 1 April, handsets no longer needed the Korean platform built in.

events.title: iPhone launches on KT
events.note: Queues formed 26 hours early for the first 1,000 units; pre-orders approached 65,000.

events.title: KakaoTalk launches
events.note: Free messaging over data begins displacing paid SMS.

events.title: LG U+ formed
events.note: LG Telecom, Dacom and Powercom merge into a third national operator.

events.title: LTE goes commercial
events.note: SK Telecom and LG U+ switch on 4G.

events.title: Nate and Cyworld breached
events.note: Roughly 35 million accounts exposed.

events.title: Shutdown Law takes effect
events.note: From 20 November, under-16s blocked from online games between midnight and 6am. Korea was the first country to try it.

events.title: World's fastest at 17.5 Mbps
events.note: Akamai puts Korea first globally; the United States is thirteenth at 5.8 Mbps.

events.title: Real-name system struck down
events.note: On 23 August the Constitutional Court rules unanimously that mandatory identity verification violates free expression.

events.title: 2010Hun-Ma47 decided
events.note: The Court found the public benefit too small to justify the restriction, and noted users had simply moved to foreign sites.

events.title: Netflix enters Korea
events.note: Foreign streaming arrives on a network already built for it.

events.title: 5G goes commercial
events.note: Korea claims the world's first nationwide consumer 5G launch.

events.title: Schools move online
events.note: The pandemic pushes education onto the network and empties the PC bangs.

events.title: Squid Game released
events.note: Korean production reaches a global audience through foreign distribution.

events.title: KT nationwide outage
events.note: A routing error cuts service to 16.5 million customers for about 40 minutes, stopping online classes, card payments and clinic records.

events.title: What the outage reached
events.note: Around 14.3 million people relied on KT for internet service as of March 2021.

events.title: Government moves to scrap the curfew
events.note: Two ministries announce the Shutdown Law will go, ten years on, replaced by a parental choice system.

events.title: Gaming curfew ends
events.note: From midnight on 31 December the decade-old shutdown is abolished. Mobile games, by then 54% of the market, were never covered by it.

events.title: Speed ranking slips to 34th
events.note: Once second in the world for fixed broadband, Korea is overtaken.

events.title: Median fixed speed hits 233 Mbps
events.note: Up 47.9% in a single year, on Ookla's measure.
